findings.title: Captured skid budget ignores drag and creates reverse skid
findings.claim: Stabilise continues subtracting the original skid after drag has already removed part of it, driving sideways velocity through zero.
findings.evidence: plan L778 captures the initial sideways speed; L782-L783 subtract only the assist correction from that budget, while L791-L792 independently apply drag to velocity. A Node arithmetic reproduction with heading 0, vx=300, gravity/edge disabled and default stabilise/drag ends after 225 ticks with skidBudget=0 but vx=-58.27445181038878. Spec L125 requires the released ship to stop skidding.
findings.why: The assist creates substantial sideways motion in the opposite direction, then stops correcting it. The existing 60 u/s test tolerates the smaller overshoot of approximately -3.06 u/s.
findings.fix: Apply the drag multiplier to the remaining captured skid budget as well as velocity, preserving the separation from later gravitational acceleration. Add a no-field regression with a substantial initial skid that asserts the sideways velocity never reverses and reaches zero when the budget is exhausted.

prior.note: plan L777-L790 now captures skid only at release and applies the assist before gravity. The amended spec L125 describes this mechanic; plan L642-L663 adds gravity and capture regressions. The separate drag regression introduced by this fix is reported above.

plan L962-L965 resolves ship 0 statics, the pair once, then ship 1 statics, matching spec L75. The regression at L893-L899 distinguishes the previous order: ship 1 moves to y=-88.5 before its planet correction to y=-90.
plan L630-L636 now asserts heading plus headingAcc after 60 turning ticks for every Engines level. Arithmetic checks produce the expected 106.66666666666667, 64 and 26.666666666666668 steps.
